![IMG_7259.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqQPZt1s7D8MDxwQm3riJ5952JJX11Cd4FEtaRTe26tHa6tvGdRQMyWXP5uAo52q54N.jpeg)*Team bonding in front of Meares Glacier. It was tough work, but we finally made it to the face of a glacier. We had been iced out until now this trip. You can see the pure joy in the guests' faces as they posed for this picture.*

   Today's adventure was one of the guests and crew favorites. We were at Meares Glacier, in northern Prince William Sound, where a massive glacier tumbles out of the tall mountains and flows into the end of a beautiful fjord. It is a rarity among glaciers these days, in that it is one of the few that is currently advancing. It is bulldozing its way through the forest, taking old trees down as it goes. It also dumps an amazing amount of ice into the fjord, which is what made this morning's kayak such an adventure. 
 
  Kayaking is always a great way to experience a tidewater glacier, and sometimes you have to pick your way through a little bit of ice, but today was an exception. We had so much ice, that our paddles would just skip across it instead of dipping down in the water. The ice packed in around us the farther we got, but onward we pushed. Sometimes I would look behind and see that I had made a nice path through the ice for the guests. Other times, when I looked, the ice move back in so fast that there was no path at all. Luckily the group was up for the challenge, and they were rewarded with a truly wild, Alaskan experience. These are the days that you remember, and tell stories about, long after getting home. 

Once we finally had enough of working hard in the ice, we found a pocket of clear water, and just sat and soaked in the amazing views. Its times like this that it is so hard to believe that we have this place all to ourselves. That is Alaska, still true wilderness to be explored. That can be hard to find these days. When we made it back to the boat, it was hot beverages for all, and a change into bathing suits.... for the polar plunge was next! 

Never a dull moment on the Safari Explorer.

![IMG_7246.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Ep1XsEkPk5m6nB99zZocapRqgX8FLLzBQVdjchcvB1gHPSbqXLfdcaBiPn5zsPi62hS.jpeg)*Paddling through the ice here at Meares Glacier is a wild, adventurous feat. You can blast right through the small chunks, but you need good navigation to avoid the bigger pieces. They will stop you in your tracks very quickly.*

![IMG_7267.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqSVyW3TJRMYTzug4Xe8Fhoh2hst7iCFEqVjcGqGEyMcgLB4LZjbX1QbPwHhF5YfUj3.jpeg)*A little drizzle didn't stop my group from kayaking across the fjord to Meares Glacier, a tidewater glacier that calves off giant chunks of ice.*

![IMG_7264.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqHzpAWL5DmSJZWoHVHrs7qoJoSoe1eUQT33aXnSUtLLuNZ52rwmyQ9yBG3TNEgnR9m.jpeg)*We had been paddling through ice for a while before finally breaking free into this section. It seemed almost too easy after what I put them through.*



![IMG_7254.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqQNWvxzfZdZyTZZKrHFk4eurtU18EguQEMPcPnbakQuU84RnbnKkmoDdrPPibLp6sb.jpeg)*Always say, 'yes', when asked if you want to kayak in front of a glacier.*

![IMG_7253.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Ep1VVeCBMeNvHPri1brsmBKCRgoLWqQZWMrGiVLijjwg5CxcSrc9T5Hbcod5CXKC8gG.jpeg)*Our skiff tour pushed even farther ahead this morning. They enjoyed some really nice calvings when pieces of ice fell a hundred feet off the face of Meares Glacier.*

![IMG_7250.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Eqd8zURRYN74mhPL5KGggEvKgtgahVDq4sAsuCDs2wy2pKsddVdnk8vQa4GcMPyH9po.jpeg)*At some points in this morning kayak, we stopped paddling and just took everything in.*

![IMG_7247.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Ep5kERtAgvWPwBkBYG7nDQjPA64dkbn3h83XzKmxZVfaGfsWz6GkFTKak7FTYno8PFW.jpeg)*The ice started to pack together pretty densely towards the end of our paddle across the fjord. I really made these guys work for it today.*



![IMG_7244.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EpnCiemCVTLuhaHzD3ZdQhJx6m3UzxC9AFjUrkHLSuCbrHtpmB1dXrLu3zbVqqLQzCV.jpeg)*Taking a break from our ice kayaking to take some photos.*

![IMG_7239.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Eq36YXwaw53YfFyFZsVjuqt4ZHyv6dHsdodxUJJmW8XdnwVnLiVp1UASXy5qEJu388p.jpeg)*This kind of ice was quite easy to make it through. It got thicker though, shortly after.*

![IMG_7238.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EnaZDJwe2Q7kE6n4PTBV9SwnQ8yQvS7C2ZZt2WX72AZSbQUTjJEKC9iiv9t52SSsH8T.jpeg)*Kayaking is one of my favorite ways to experience Alaska. This morning, at Meares Glacier, was an absolute blast. We kayaked through so much ice, and made it close enough to watch ice calving off the face of the glacier. Sea otters and seals looked on, as kittiwakes flew overhead. Luckily our rain gear held solid, and the old saying, 'there is no such thing as bad weather, only bad clothing', held true.*

![IMG_7235.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Eou8EtoSqD8fMHBNUxHEt3aGr5F2fA8W6dmYRQc4ypMKSqDU2wjyoozQ6t4TXHsdVP6.jpeg)*Meares is a unique glacier in that it is advancing, bulldozing the forest as it goes.*

![IMG_7234.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/244e85EMEmgz8HNNP2RL54f2SqA3XQ23UxFLS4Fn1Hg8QRYMe2RQgCLesJEF6apwhbB1k.jpeg)*Meares panorama.*

![IMG_7232.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EoyPZAe1DXp4GRJGCf6TyPEBApRybGKFtYhsCC2uPyZvg19E8A9UxYPBBHTyqFraArE.jpeg)*Rain, ice, and rainforest.*

![IMG_7231.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Eq9UnvYdrjauzzyC9zfG4jXFtZdGYVR9SBACEgzECqXfjgKeLsg3cjegGUC6W5NyPm6.jpeg)*The mist hung to the tops of the forest trees as we made our way through acres of ice.*

![IMG_7226.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqL7k5isi3yKA7EYUhHeSCQFuVYUkQtAhbCK3uMW1d2iEgyh5yEbd3n4rYLRdyiJSp3.jpeg)*Chris and Alan soaking in the rain, and the views.*

![IMG_7225.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EqFs1czockctH6oWpQFSVxQHiTypWgvyVnKxmJx1UReowgXnomuSGoWyLFnEmwChszG.jpeg)*Ice, ice and more ice.*

![IMG_7222.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EoAaDvmNUnZ3c5Hg73v48kXFr74N2XmHRaaEkMctNeFBUQzUc4Tzw3Uqq5stNgLQh3u.jpeg)*Just keep paddling.*

![IMG_7209.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/EoK6p8i9KtutJWFoivpg5wy9Mze8BzRvksdwU1MvbrtD73hQpfULtc5EBZ3TGNjJeqf.jpeg)*Sending out kayakers at Meares Glacier in Prince William Sound.*

![IMG_7203.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/Eq38TUxWSf1RNZS98G84seRosHySFWv8yqw4Tx6aXP6DVzSuPsXg6xAQCMrtu12aHhp.jpeg)*Me, guiding the morning kayak, ready for some icy adventure.*

![IMG_7199.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dtam/242DJWW6dsCntiWSTJCnBqc3HWoqu6sgbbpSubFggrgneKRvihJtR1tEn93c4pTDne3uJ.jpeg)*This seems like true expedition cruising doesn't it. Definitely not your big cruise ship vibe.*

As always, keep traveling and keep posting.

![mac property.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xVMEJGF7DkvNnSF2M6yWp8mCCtjDgsguG1HaQ8ShWGPYRN9brCw3UWHKzuBdsD7ZYx4.png)
There are quite a number of volcanic mountain in East-Java including the famous ones such as Bromo and Semeru but actually, there are many older volcanic mountain in the region that is dormant and worth exploring, such as Mount Wilis. Unlike the popular hike in the region, Mt. Wilis is not commercialized due to its access that are still challenging and raw. If you enjoy quiter hike and untounched trails, this is one of the place to be. Last Saturday, I got the opportunity to visit deeper part of the foothills to experience shallot harversting. A close friend of my mother owned a few hectares of farmlands tucked away deep in the mountain. I heard from their son that it was harvest season, so I immeditely volunteered for the adventure. ![DSCF1948.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23wWu6rYofQxgsjbwJxPGBy24VstHhmT3Zf9GQynbh72B9LyXPVVVgKSi19VjsU5tT2Re.JPG) We started the journey at 5 AM with regular car then switch to different car fitting for the mountain rough terrain. On our way to the harvest area, we passed through thick jungle where it feels like we were sandwiched between the lush greenery and the dangling roots all around it. Somewhere along the winding path, The son of the family started telling me that there was a famous coffee plantation and factory in the area. He pointed to the remnants of the factory as well as some abandoned villa all around these foothills of Mt. Wilis. One thing that came out of my mouth was " How did they even know this place existed?", considering it was ages ago and even today this place is still considered remote. ![DSCF1950.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23vsQDEB1ar6wcuDhdGoEbSA5YmDaSu6Ft3Y7e8haaVNiXvWLL2bnsBzn86kczX6mtoq5.JPG) So, how did the dutch even scouted it? Whoever did that back in the day certainly has no fear of anything. I also heard that today, you can still find a lively wild animals animal including smaller sized tiger once in a while. As we pressed on, our 30 minutes bumpy ride, eventually come to a fruition. We started seeing rows of shallots. ![DSCF1956.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/245cWZREnfTi9gkwQQ226ZhSEQwww3gKLW12jCen8WkmKNQjWHJ6JMSSFbeApo59yQT3o.JPG) The family owns the biggest hut in the area. Practically, you can live there as it has a room, a bathroom, a common kitchen with a view like this. ![DSCF2044.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23qrBx5QDH2m7R4y7pWjH5bDgWEMJP9AYxg7LUYNZtPxcwpYSc5Je75kLte4nEpNekD1V.JPG) Before we start the harvest, the workers and us had the chance to fuel oursevles with packed lunch. They also served me a coffee, famous from the region. It was good! ![DSCF1981.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/244ofQkQqsAR5wv8Y74hkPDTthivZqVMgq9JRJ45AdckHnJobKU3xh7A7kz9n21XgRYGt.JPG) ![DSCF1988.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23ywyiXpEuhd4cCYKN7ALMbsZTDdiz7YPikedz2R3yfpLoXNZFapSuhrnaP6ThkvxPeZn.JPG) I walked around further to explore the trails all around the places. Locals told me about different paths we could take to explore it as well as places we we could do bike trails. So, I walked around because they don't need me to harvest yet. I found these beautiful spots all around the area that looks so untounched and raw. ![DSCF2078.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/244eCfGKqKVL4yABFAHJD5repNvJYrZQiEj2ZFGAKYK4civERhkJ7XrYRyGDiuvM6k2QP.JPG) ![DSCF2085.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23s9TKcJvENbeai8xpjRpmajArXtreXfKmpw7zGC8oy2CCXbypcQW411tjgFAAKHJiRBR.JPG) After I got tired exploring around, I joined the workers to pick shallots, filling up the bag with laughters filled the air to pass the time. It was really fun to pluck out the shallots and do the harvest.
![DSCF2090.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23uQnVtVUz6854uHLoZKj7GXuhCztM7tkegm24uXMKie8nvgHrTHnNRZY5dvqA7KWT3ph.JPG)
![DSCF2034.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23yJLysBiWcShvJPdCsDFJuaEwrzgzhsfWgq4nk9ryzuBPrEXjyPbkiTaTrqvC9SzPxxH.JPG)
This is once in a lifetime opportunity for me to experience this activity. After some rest, I took pictures of the workers who was waiting for lunch time. ![DSCF2101.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23xpCmxNn1hwyp8nvmNGWhR3DFzBBZewPzNVpWcrTfscFgbonkr5mKeStR3PxqmXsf6S6.JPG) Once we finished the row in the back of the hut, I explored another rows in front of it there's this beautiful blooming flowers of shallots. ![DSCF2067.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23tbnq6j1QQhyAEaosCNTZRHG8vQyNQBqTzvYC1FbqQQ3S8LXWL1NL3Fth12Uix29npPr.JPG) The mist started to appear during noon and it was time for us to also go down from the mountain. It was my first time exploring this mountain and didn't know it was hikeable at first. If you enjoy hiking or trekking, this is one of the most underrated, untounched places in East-Java and around. Many people who passes this city don't even know this place existed, including myself. This is why, I wondered how did they dutch even found it and built an empire of coffee plantation in this region? ![DSCF2152.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/246GBHrM84d9wPKMfqovUq9EJpk21RzSvB4HgLkGGJER8Qax77W8wjynjBFAfFWCS3yoP.JPG) This was the adventure that left me with more questions than answer. I wanted to go back there again and hoping I could get another chance to visit and explore more of the area. I saw some waterfalls around it that I didn't get the chance to look at. On the map, this place is also called Mt Liman too ( which is the highest peak of it) and the Mt Wilis itself is the name of the mountain range of the area because it connects several places in the region. Maybe it's time to explore your own city and who know, just as I do, finding this spot that looks so mesmerizing I came to know though I frequented this city. ||| |-|- ![NTy4GV6ooFRmaCXZ8UYgPhoud1kjiNX8QokLEZtbBKLuLWQ9yt7K3o4PG7qiS2SfyUvr6dYces7DWJ8xfHhq8PVtQPrvofyP72KL3ppdRxeugWvBfxeBRgtHv4FSStZc4YZ6Tzt1Pm995NNPZRyGjU7WNd7xvdEv2qtUNXuG.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/macchiata/23t77FQVTCGtEBi1QzCfnjLFZ3BpB57ocvnKWNZbybVoNT2WGNztX9UKrTyCVdjXyPVch.jpg)|

After having been surrounded by travelers from all over the world, I discovered just how valuable the City of Buenos Aires is from a tourism perspective. Perhaps as locals we do not pay much attention to it, but our area is full of interesting places to visit and explore. When I returned from my last backpacking trip, I decided to explore those corners of the city that others appreciate so much, with the goal of continuing to learn more about my own province. One of those places was the area surrounding the famous Boca Juniors stadium, and I found a neighborhood full of life and passion for football 😃.
Después de haber estado rodeada de viajeros de todas partes, descubrí lo valiosa que es la Ciudad de Buenos Aires a nivel turístico. Quizás como locales no prestamos tanta atención a esto, pero nuestra zona está llena de lugares interesantes para ir a visitar y recorrer. Cuando volví de mi último viaje de mochilera, me decidí a explorar esos rincones de la ciudad que otros valoran tantos, con el objetivo de seguir conociendo un poco más de mi propia provincia. Uno de esos puntos era el que rodea la famosa cancha de Boca Juniors, y me encontré con un barrio lleno de vida y pasión por el fútbol 😃.
--- ---
--- --- While looking through the city’s tourist attractions, I realized there are so many places I still do not know, and now I have a long list of outings pending. One of them was the iconic neighborhood of La Boca. Of course, I had heard about it before, but I did not even know where it was located until one weekend when I decided to find out. Getting there took my sisters and me a one-hour train ride and another 20 minutes by bus. We traveled 30 kilometers before arriving, but we are used to these kinds of distances whenever it means seeing something beautiful.
Revisando un poco la oferta turística de la ciudad, me di cuenta de que hay un montón de lugares que no conozco, y ahora tengo una larga lista de paseos pendientes. Uno de ellos era hasta el emblemático barrio de La Boca. Por supuesto que había escuchado hablar de él, pero ni siquiera sabía en donde queda, hasta que un fin de semana me decidí a averiguarlo. Llegar hasta él nos tomó a mis hermanas y a mí, un viaje de una hora en tren y otros 20 minutos en bus. Viajamos 30 kilómetros hasta que llegamos, pero estamos acostumbradas a estas distancias con tal de ver algo lindo.
---
--- As expected, the neighborhood of La Boca was full of tourists, mainly because it is home to one of the classic postcards of a trip to Buenos Aires: the famous Caminito. But before stopping there for our photo session, we decided to explore the surrounding area a bit. I had heard comments saying that you have to move around this neighborhood carefully because once you get away from the tourist center, it stops feeling so friendly. However, at the time of our visit, everything looked lively and safe.
Como era de esperarse, el barrio de La Boca estaba lleno de turistas, principalmente porque ahí se encuentra una de las postales típicas de tu viaje a Buenos Aires: el famoso Caminito. Pero antes de detenernos ahí y hacer la sesión de fotos, decidimos explorar un poco los alrededores. Yo había escuchado comentarios de que hay que moverse por este barrio con cuidado, porque al alejarse del centro turístico ya no se vuelve tan amigable, pero para el momento de nuestra visita todo se veía animado y seguro.
---
--- When we left behind all the hustle and bustle of the crowds and souvenir shops, we arrived at the Boca Juniors stadium. This massive stadium, known as La Bombonera, is unmistakable because of its blue and yellow colors, and every matchday it gathers thousands of supporters. But it was not only the stadium painted in those colors — all the shops around it were as well. People have transformed these streets and businesses into true works of art that attract fans from everywhere. Everything looked so picturesque; I loved the area and seeing how the football atmosphere can truly be felt in that corner of La Boca.
Cuando salimos de todo el ajetreo de gente y tiendas de souvenirs, llegamos hasta la cancha de Boca Juniors. Este gran estadio, llamado La Bombonera, es inconfundible por sus colores azul y amarillo, y cada fecha reúne a miles de seguidores. Pero no solo la cancha estaba pintada así, sino también todas las tiendas de sus alrededores. La gente transformó estas calles y negocios en verdaderas obras de arte que atraen fanáticos. Era todo muy pintoresco, me encantó la zona y ver que el ambiente de futbol se respira en ese rincón de La Boca.
---
--- Club Atlético Boca Juniors is one of the biggest football clubs in Argentina. Its classic rival is Club Atlético River Plate, whose colors are white and red. When it comes to opposites, people will always ask, “Boca or River?”, usually getting almost the same number of answers in favor of one team or the other. Apparently, this rivalry has reached an international level, because many tourists also come to Buenos Aires with the dream of watching a match between the two, commonly known as “El Superclásico.” Of course, there is also a huge business surrounding all of this, with ticket prices reaching ridiculously high levels, yet still always selling out completely. During this visit, simply seeing the stadium from the outside was more than enough for me 😂.
El Club Atlético Boca Juniors es uno de los equipos de futbol más grandes de Argentina. Su rival clásico es Club Atlético River Plate, con sus colores blanco y rojo. Cuando se trata de opuestos, uno siempre preguntaría "¿Boca o River?", teniendo casi igual de respuestas a favor de un equipo u otro. Aparentemente, esta rivalidad escala internacionalmente, porque muchos turistas también llegan a Buenos Aires con la ilusión de ver un partido de ambos, normalmente llamado "El Superclásico". Por supuesto que también existe el gran negocio alrededor de todo esto, donde hay una venta de entradas a niveles ridículamente elevados, pero que siempre se terminan vendiendo por completo. En esta visita, ver la cancha desde afuera fue suficiente para mí 😂.
---
---
--- Visiting the area around the Club Atlético Boca Juniors stadium was an outing that made me feel a little like a tourist in Buenos Aires. I really enjoyed seeing this whole atmosphere, which felt very friendly, at least during the time of my visit. I imagine that on match days this place must become absolutely packed with people in good spirits, an experience I would also love to have someday, especially if it included actually going inside the stadium. As for me, if someone asks, “River or Boca?”, I will always choose Boca because my family supports this team. I do not know much about football when it comes to Boca, but I still firmly stick to that side 😅.

# How to Run a Digital Agency Solo: 4 Systems That Replace a Full Team

Most clients don't care how many people work at your agency. They care whether their phone rings, whether their posts go up, and whether you pick up when they call. That's the whole game — and one person can absolutely play it, if they're running the right systems.

Here's what actually works.

---

## 1. One Client Onboarding Doc That Does All the Heavy Lifting

The first two weeks with a new client are the most labor-intensive. You're collecting logos, passwords, photos, logins, preferences, and backstory. If you're doing this by email thread, you're wasting hours.

Build a single onboarding form — Google Forms or Notion works fine. Include every question you'd normally ask over three separate conversations: brand colors, posting preferences, services offered, the owner's name and how they want to be credited, the link to their Google Business profile. One link. They fill it out once. You pull from it for the next 12 months.

This one change eliminates the "remind me what your hours are again" back-and-forth and makes you look like you've done this a hundred times — even if this is client number two.

---

## 2. A Content Queue That Runs Ahead of Schedule

The single biggest mistake solo operators make is producing content the same week it needs to go out. That puts you one bad week away from missing a post, and clients notice missed posts faster than they notice good ones.

The fix is simple: stay three to four weeks ahead. Every time you sit down to write for a client, write two weeks' worth instead of one. It sounds like more work but it's actually less — you get into the client's voice, you're not context-switching back and forth, and you build a buffer that covers holidays, sick days, and busy seasons.

If you're using an AI writing tool (and you should be), batch the drafts in one session, then spend 20 minutes editing to put the client's real voice back in. Their phrases, their slang, the way they talk about their food or their products. That's the 20% of work that makes the other 80% worth anything.

---

## 3. A Dead-Simple Reporting Template Clients Actually Read

Clients who feel informed don't churn. Clients who feel like they're throwing money into a black hole do.

You don't need a fancy dashboard. A monthly email with five numbers — follower count this month vs. last, top-performing post, how many new reviews came in, website traffic if you have it, and one thing you're testing next month — is enough to keep a local business owner engaged and confident.

The key word is *one thing you're testing next month.* It signals that you're thinking ahead, not just executing. It also gives you an easy opening line for next month's report. Clients love feeling like they're part of a strategy.

Template this. Fill in the blanks every month. Send it on the same day every month. That consistency alone puts you ahead of most freelancers.

---

## 4. Boundaries That Protect the 20% Only You Can Do

Systems handle the repeatable work. But there's a category of work only you can do: deciding what content strategy to pursue, handling a client crisis, landing a new account. If you let client check-ins and revision requests eat into that time, you stop growing.

Set response windows and communicate them upfront. Something like: "I check messages at 10am and 3pm on weekdays. For anything urgent, text me." Most clients won't have an emergency in the first six months. The ones who do will respect the boundary more than they resent it.

Also: invoice on a fixed day. Don't chase payments. Set up auto-invoicing, even if it's just a recurring Google Calendar reminder to send a Stripe link. Getting paid on schedule removes a layer of anxiety that drains more energy than it looks like.

---

## The Bottom Line

Running a digital agency solo isn't about pretending to be bigger than you are. It's about building systems tight enough that clients feel the consistency of a full team, even when it's just you with good tools and a clear schedule.

The agencies that fail at one person aren't understaffed. They're undersystemized. Fix the systems and the size stops mattering.

The crypto world was much simpler back in 2009 when all that existed was Bitcoin. We had a single token (BTC) with a maximum supply of 21 million.

In 2026, tens of thousands of new tokens are launched daily across various blockchains. Most are short-lived memecoins, while a growing share power innovative [AI agents](https://inleo.io/@brennanhm/can-ai-agents-save-the-crypto-market-7cc).

https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVVdQZnno7hsAKRFw9Tggmm5V6DVbfvL1rXSrJfECBhHk/bankr_ecosystem.jpg

In today's article, we are going to briefly cover the history of crypto token creation, as well as Bankr's expanding AI agent ecosystem.

# Token Creation

Ethereum launched in July 2015, enabling anyone to write smart contracts and create their own tokens. At the time, token creation was entirely manual. There were no easy token launchpads.

The process of launching a token has been simplified since then, especially with the launch of pump.fun on Solana in early 2024, which allowed anyone to create a token (often a [memecoin](https://inleo.io/@brennanhm/are-we-underestimating-the-power-of-meme-coins)) with the click of a button.

The advent of AI agents inspired even more innovation.

# Virtuals Launchpad

The Virtuals launchpad was built on Base (Ethereum Layer 2) in early 2024. Virtuals pioneered the model of allocating a portion of trading fees from creator/AI agent tokens to self-fund resources like inference/compute.

- Uses a 1% trading fee on agent tokens.  
- Pre-graduation (bonding curve phase): 100% of fees typically go to the protocol treasury.
- Post-graduation: Roughly 70% goes to the creator/founder (but often locked or subject to thresholds, with periodic releases).

# Bankr Launchpad

Bankr, an AI agent launchpad which launched in late 2024, took inspiration from Virtuals, but innovated in a few ways:

Good evening, blog friends, I'm back with you to take you to a lovely little place I visited a few days ago, Traversagna or Margine dicoperta, a charming place located near Montecatini, near Buggiano and Santa Lucia, which I'll tell you about soon. Honestly, I only knew about this place because there's a famous music club here where they hold many concerts and jam sessions, but I'd never visited the surrounding area. This place is located in the Nievole plain, bordering the Fucecchio Marshes (another place I'd like to visit soon). Traversagna is a small village with medieval origins. Today, it's a passageway, divided between the houses on the main street, some neighboring streets, and the countryside, including some bordering the marshes. It's a very quiet and pleasant place. In ancient times, it's said that there were hospices here that housed pilgrims on their way to Lucca, as was the case in almost all the towns in the area that were a stopover for pilgrims. Instead, until the mid-1900s it was a predominantly rural area still to be reclaimed and urbanized, but little by little, with the growth of cities and urbanization, it became a residential, urban and completely or almost completely reclaimed area.

> Buenas noches, amigos del blog, estoy de vuelta para llevarlos a un pequeño y encantador lugar que visité hace unos días, Traversagna o Margine dicoperta, un lugar con encanto ubicado cerca de Montecatini, cerca de Buggiano y Santa Lucia, del que les hablaré pronto. Este lugar está ubicado en la llanura de Nievole, limitando con las Marismas de Fucecchio (otro lugar que me gustaría visitar pronto). Traversagna es un pequeño pueblo de origen medieval. Hoy en día, es un pasaje, dividido entre las casas de la calle principal, algunas calles vecinas y el campo, incluyendo algunas que limitan con las marismas. Es un lugar muy tranquilo y agradable. En la antigüedad, se dice que aquí había hospicios que alojaban a los peregrinos en su camino a Lucca, como ocurría en casi todos los pueblos de la zona que eran parada para los peregrinos. En cambio, hasta mediados del siglo XX era una zona predominantemente rural que aún estaba por recuperar y urbanizar, pero poco a poco, con el crecimiento de las ciudades y la urbanización, se convirtió en una zona residencial, urbana y total o casi totalmente recuperada.

Continuing on, however, we return to a more industrialized area, a little less beautiful than the green spaces, but still with several tree-lined avenues, so not all concrete! Here too, there are villas and shops, mostly factories, but I'm not sure what. In any case, it's a small village that I quite enjoyed, even though it doesn't have any major highlights. It's a pleasant little Tuscan town, typical of the area. See you soon with more trips, blogging friends!
